sections.title: Application
sections.description: Create the application object directly or through a factory.

snippets.code:
import os

from flask import Flask

def create_app(test_config=None):
    app = Flask(__name__, instance_relative_config=True)
    os.makedirs(app.instance_path, exist_ok=True)
    app.config.from_mapping(
        SECRET_KEY=os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY", "dev-only"),
        DATABASE=os.path.join(app.instance_path, "app.sqlite"),
    )

    # FLASK_SECRET_KEY, FLASK_DATABASE, ... override the defaults
    app.config.from_prefixed_env()

    if test_config is not None:
        app.config.update(test_config)

    return app

sections.title: Request
sections.description: Read query strings, JSON bodies, forms and uploaded files.

snippets.code:
from pathlib import Path

from flask import Flask, request
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["UPLOAD_FOLDER"] = Path("uploads")
app.config["UPLOAD_FOLDER"].mkdir(exist_ok=True)

@app.post("/upload")
def upload():
    title = request.form["title"]  # a missing field raises 400
    note = request.form.get("note", "")
    file = request.files.get("attachment")
    if file is None or file.filename == "":
        return {"error": "attachment is required"}, 400
    target = app.config["UPLOAD_FOLDER"] / secure_filename(file.filename)
    file.save(target)
    return {"title": title, "note": note, "saved_as": target.name}, 201

sections.title: Database
sections.description: Store models with Flask-SQLAlchemy and query them with SQLAlchemy 2.

snippets.code:
from flask import Flask
from flask_sqlalchemy import SQLAlchemy
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, mapped_column

class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    pass

db = SQLAlchemy(model_class=Base)

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI"] = "sqlite:///library.db"
db.init_app(app)

class Book(db.Model):
    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(db.String(120), nullable=False)
    year: Mapped[int | None]

with app.app_context():
    db.create_all()  # switch to migrations once the schema changes

sections.title: Testing
sections.description: Drive the app through the test client with pytest fixtures.

snippets.code:
# tests/test_api.py
def test_home_page(client):
    response = client.get("/")
    assert response.status_code == 200

def test_create_article(client):
    response = client.post("/articles", json={"title": "A short note"})
    assert response.status_code == 201
    assert response.get_json() == {"created": True}

def test_dashboard_redirects_anonymous_user(client):
    response = client.get("/dashboard")
    assert response.status_code == 302
    assert response.headers["Location"].startswith("/login")

def test_seeded_session_reaches_dashboard(client):
    with client.session_transaction() as session:
        session["user_email"] = "ada@example.com"
    response = client.get("/dashboard")
    assert response.status_code == 200

sections.title: Deployment
sections.description: Run the app under Gunicorn, preferably inside a container.

snippets.code:
# wsgi.py
from app import create_app

application = create_app()

# Production server in the same environment as the application
pip install "gunicorn>=23.0"

# Four workers behind a reverse proxy on the same host
gunicorn --workers 4 --bind 127.0.0.1:8000 --access-logfile - wsgi:application

# Reload the workers after deploying new code (the oldest match is the master)
kill -HUP "$(pgrep -o -f 'gunicorn.*wsgi:application')"

FROM python:3.13-slim

ENV PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
    PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1

WORKDIR /srv
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .
RUN useradd --create-home app && chown -R app:app /srv
USER app

EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["gunicorn", "--workers", "4", "--bind", "0.0.0.0:8000", "wsgi:application"]
